summary: Add html_attrs() to render a dict as HTML attributes, for templates that build tags from data. It is also available inside SimpleTemplate templates.
behaviour: `bottle.html_attrs(attrs)` renders the dict `attrs` as HTML attributes in the dict's order, each written as a space, the name, `="`, the escaped value and `"`: `html_attrs({'title': 'Hi', 'id': 'go'})` gives ` title="Hi" id="go"`. An empty dict gives an empty string.
Names lose their trailing underscores and the remaining `_` become `-`: `class_` is written as `class`, `data_user_id` as `data-user-id`.
`True` writes the bare name (` disabled`); `False` and `None` leave the attribute out. Every other value, `0` and `''` included, is written.

A list or tuple value is joined with single spaces (`{'class_': ['btn', 'big']}` gives ` class="btn big"`); other values are converted with `str()`. Values are escaped with `html_escape()`, so `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` and `'` are replaced and everything else, line breaks and tabs included, is written as it is.
A name that is empty after the conversion, or contains whitespace, a quote, `<`, `>`, `/`, `=` or a control character, raises `ValueError`.
Inside SimpleTemplate templates `html_attrs` is available without an import, as in `<input{{!html_attrs(attrs)}}>`.

entries: - Changed: html_escape() takes quote=False to leave quotes alone and converts non-string values with str(), and html_quote() is removed. (feature/5b70e2)
- Added: bottle.__all__ lists the public API, so `from bottle import *` brings in only public names. (feature/c3a18e)

entry: - Added: html_attrs() renders a dict as HTML attributes, also inside SimpleTemplate templates. ({branch})
